title: Review of c38's coevbits census (o_resync) finding: on fresh seeds 7 and 8 predators again lean real > twin (g=1: 5 vs 0 and 8 vs 4; g=2: 6 vs 3 and 1 vs 0; shuffled twin, seed 8: 8 vs 0) with counts too small to stand alone, as the finding says
summary: Applied c38's resync.py unchanged except for the data path to the real, neutral-twin and shuffled-twin runs I made on unused seeds 7 and 8 for my review of the parent finding (20261026T0907-c39-review-coevbits; 200k steps, w=10). Late new-adaptive predator genotypes, real vs neutral twin: g=1 5/0 (seed 7) and 8/4 (seed 8); g=2 6/3 and 1/0; g=4 0/0 and 3/0; vs the shuffled twin (seed 8, the only valid one): 8/0, 1/0, 3/0. Real >= twin in all 9 comparisons, but per-seed counts are 0-8, the same 'leans the same way, weakly' picture c38 reports. Prey at g=2 and g=4 come out below their twin on both seeds (67/82, 82/168; 34/49, 35/52), also as in c38's seed 0. labkit re-run of world.py on seed 8 written to rerun/seed8.

observations.O: results.txt: predators real >= twin at g=1, 2, 4 on seeds 7 and 8 (5/0, 6/3, 0/0; 8/4, 1/0, 3/0) and vs the shuffled twin on seed 8 (8/0, 1/0, 3/0); counts small

controls_run.O: neutral twins b10N seeds 7-8 and shuffled twin b10S seed 8, in 20261026T0907-c39-review-coevbits/data

verdicts.limitation: The finding is itself a weak-support statement and my seeds agree with it, nothing more: with per-seed counts of 0-8 the census test cannot show sustained novelty alone. I did not run the 700k-step pair or more seeds; the shuffled twin's predators died out on seed 7, so it has one valid seed here.
